answer.rationale: The two acute symptoms are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), which points at the funnel rather than at price. Promotional pricing is the tempting response to the competitor, but memory_73 is the one inherited record with a clean negative: +31% signups and +18% revenue bought with -12% retention and no renewal lift, which is the opposite of sustainable qualified revenue. Referral incentives (memory_57) work on established customers and would not touch the failing top-of-funnel; enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is a different segment and does not address the SMB bleed. That leaves simplify_onboarding and activation_messaging, both plausible. I choose simplify_onboarding because two independent inherited records (memory_31 on cutting signup fields, memory_86 on shortening onboarding) point the same direction and because it acts directly on the metric that fell furthest upstream; activation messaging is the natural follow-on once accounts actually reach the product. I spend both verification pulls on exactly the memories my decision rests on: memory_31 and memory_86 are the load-bearing claims, and both are stated in unusually soft terms ('durable lift', 'lifting early adoption') with no sample size, effect size, duration, or renewal-horizon data. Verifying the direction I intend to act on is worth more than verifying memory_73, which I am using only to rule an option out and which already reports the harm I care about. Two open risks I am not resolving with this experiment. First, the downstream-value risk: cutting required signup fields can raise activation while degrading lead qualification and routing, so a completion-rate win can quietly convert into lower-quality pipeline. Both supporting memories measure early funnel metrics only, so neither one can tell me whether the lift survived to renewal; I am inferring durability I have not observed. Second, memory_44 says enterprise converts better through sales-assist, so any field-cutting must not strip the signals that route enterprise prospects to demo-request. I therefore scope this to SMB self-serve, preserve qualification and routing fields, and instrument renewal-horizon cohorts alongside completion rate rather than declaring victory on completion alone. Standard experiment scale, not broad rollout: the evidence is consistent but thin and unverified, and the competitor pressure creates exactly the urgency that would tempt an over-scaled bet.
